1. About These Terms

These Terms of Service apply to services supplied by AmplifyIQ.

AmplifyIQ contact details:

Trading as: AmplifyIQ County Mayo, Ireland Email: info@amplifyiq.ie

By accepting a quotation or proposal, paying a deposit, instructing AmplifyIQ to begin work or otherwise entering into an agreement for services, the client agrees to these Terms together with the applicable quotation, proposal or project agreement.

2. Services

AmplifyIQ provides services that may include:

  • website design;
  • website redesign;
  • landing-page design;
  • website development;
  • responsive website development;
  • digital growth services;
  • website strategy;
  • website optimisation;
  • website maintenance;
  • hosting-related assistance;
  • domain-related assistance;
  • integrations;
  • automation;
  • digital products;
  • consultancy; and
  • other related digital services agreed with the client.

The exact scope of each project will be defined in the applicable proposal, quotation, invoice, statement of work or written agreement.

3. Quotations and Proposals

Unless stated otherwise, quotations are based on the information available at the time they are issued.

A quotation applies only to the work specifically described within it.

Additional requests or changes that materially increase the scope of a project may result in additional charges.

Where there is a conflict between these Terms and a specifically negotiated written project proposal, the specifically negotiated project term will take priority for that project.

4. Pricing

Prices are as stated in the applicable quotation or proposal.

Any applicable VAT, third-party charges, domain fees, software subscriptions, hosting charges, advertising spend, stock-media costs or other external costs will be identified separately where reasonably possible.

Unless expressly included in a quotation, third-party fees are not included in AmplifyIQ's project price.

5. Deposits and Payments

A project may require an upfront deposit before work begins.

The required deposit and payment schedule will be specified in the relevant proposal, quotation or invoice.

Unless otherwise agreed in writing:

  • work may not begin until the required initial payment has been received;
  • milestone payments become due when the relevant milestone is reached;
  • final payment must be made before final ownership transfer, handover or unrestricted release of completed project files;
  • AmplifyIQ may pause work where an invoice becomes overdue; and
  • project deadlines may move where work is paused because of late payment.

Invoices must be paid by the due date shown on the invoice.

6. Scope of Work

The agreed project scope will be set out in the proposal, quotation, project brief or other written agreement.

Anything not expressly included should be considered outside the original scope.

Examples of additional work may include:

  • extra pages;
  • major layout changes;
  • new functionality;
  • additional integrations;
  • major design-direction changes after approval;
  • additional copywriting;
  • additional animations;
  • additional languages;
  • custom software functionality;
  • e-commerce features not originally agreed;
  • additional rounds of revisions; and
  • work resulting from a major change in client requirements.

Additional work may be quoted separately.

7. Revisions

The number or extent of revisions included in a project will be set out in the relevant proposal or quotation.

A revision means a reasonable modification to work already created within the agreed project scope.

A revision does not include a complete change of project direction, rebuilding an approved design or introducing substantial new requirements.

Additional revisions may be charged separately.

The client agrees to provide, where applicable:

  • login credentials;

  • hosting information;
  • legal or regulatory information;
  • approvals;
  • feedback; and
  • other materials reasonably required to complete the project.

The client is responsible for ensuring that information provided to AmplifyIQ is accurate and lawful.

The client must have appropriate rights or licences to use any:

  • trademarks;
  • photographs;
  • music;
  • product information; or
  • other material supplied to AmplifyIQ.

The client agrees not to instruct AmplifyIQ to publish content that unlawfully infringes the rights of another person.

9. Client Delays

Project schedules depend upon timely feedback, content, approvals and access from the client.

Where a client delays providing required materials or decisions, project timelines may be extended.

AmplifyIQ will not be responsible for missed deadlines caused by delays outside its reasonable control, including delays caused by the client or third-party providers.

Where a project remains inactive for an extended period because the client has failed to provide necessary information or feedback, AmplifyIQ may reschedule the project according to current availability.

10. Project Timelines

Any completion date supplied by AmplifyIQ is an estimate unless expressly agreed in writing as a fixed contractual deadline.

Timelines may be affected by:

  • client response times;
  • change requests;
  • third-party services;
  • hosting providers;
  • domain providers;
  • technical issues;
  • approval delays;
  • supplier delays;
  • events beyond our reasonable control; or
  • changes in project scope.

AmplifyIQ will make reasonable efforts to communicate significant delays.

11. Approval and Launch

The client is responsible for reviewing the website before final approval or launch.

The client should review, where relevant:

  • text;
  • contact information;
  • prices;
  • images;
  • links;
  • functionality;
  • forms;
  • product information;
  • spelling;
  • legal information; and
  • business details.

Once the client approves the project for launch, the website will be considered accepted subject to any rights that cannot lawfully be excluded.

Minor defects discovered after launch should be reported within a reasonable period.

12. Website Content and Legal Compliance

Unless specifically agreed as part of a separately defined service, the client is responsible for determining the legal, regulatory and industry-specific requirements applying to the client's business and website.

This includes, where relevant:

  • privacy information;
  • cookie policies;
  • industry disclosures;
  • accessibility obligations;
  • consumer information;
  • terms of sale;
  • product claims;
  • copyright permissions; and
  • regulatory notices.

AmplifyIQ may assist with implementation of material supplied or approved by a client but does not act as the client's solicitor, accountant or regulatory adviser.

The client retains ownership of materials owned by the client before the project.

AmplifyIQ Materials

AmplifyIQ retains ownership of:

Where these materials are incorporated into a project, the client receives the rights reasonably necessary to operate the completed website, subject to applicable third-party licences.

Final Bespoke Deliverables

Unless otherwise agreed in writing, AmplifyIQ may display completed work for reasonable promotional purposes, including:

  • social-media profiles;
  • portfolio presentations;

  • sales presentations; and
  • award submissions.

Where confidentiality has been specifically agreed in writing, AmplifyIQ will respect the agreed restrictions.

15. Third-Party Software and Services

Websites commonly depend upon third-party products and services including:

  • hosting;
  • domain registrars;
  • content-management systems;
  • plugins;
  • APIs;
  • fonts;
  • payment processors;
  • email platforms;
  • analytics systems;
  • social-media services;
  • maps;

  • external software.

These services are controlled by their respective providers.

AmplifyIQ cannot guarantee that a third-party service will:

  • remain available indefinitely;
  • remain free;
  • maintain its existing pricing;
  • remain compatible with a website;
  • retain a particular feature;
  • operate without interruption; or
  • remain unchanged.

Changes required because of a third-party provider after completion of a project may be chargeable unless covered by an ongoing support agreement.

16. Domains

Where AmplifyIQ assists with domain registration or configuration, ownership of the domain should normally remain with or be transferred to the client, subject to payment and the rules of the relevant registrar.

The client is responsible for:

  • renewal fees;
  • maintaining accurate registrar information;
  • keeping account access secure; and
  • ensuring domain renewals are completed.

AmplifyIQ is not responsible for loss of a domain caused by a client's failure to renew it where AmplifyIQ was not contractually responsible for renewal.

17. Hosting

Hosting is only included where expressly stated.

Where AmplifyIQ provides or arranges hosting:

  • the scope and price of hosting will be separately agreed;
  • hosting may depend upon third-party infrastructure;
  • no hosting environment can be guaranteed to operate without interruption;
  • reasonable security measures will be used;
  • planned or emergency maintenance may occasionally be necessary; and
  • third-party outages may occur outside AmplifyIQ's control.

Where hosting is purchased directly by the client, the contractual relationship for that hosting remains between the client and the relevant provider.

18. Website Maintenance

Unless maintenance is expressly included in the agreed service, a completed website does not include unlimited future maintenance.

After handover, updates may be required because of:

  • software updates;
  • browser changes;
  • security requirements;
  • plugin changes;
  • operating-system changes;
  • third-party API changes; or
  • changes made by the client or another developer.

Future maintenance may be quoted separately.

19. Backups and Security

Where AmplifyIQ manages a website or hosting environment, reasonable precautions may be taken to protect the website and project data.

However, the client should maintain appropriate backups unless backup responsibility is specifically included within a service agreement.

No internet-connected service can be guaranteed to be entirely free from:

  • cyberattack;
  • malware;
  • unauthorised access;
  • software vulnerabilities;
  • service interruption; or
  • data loss.

20. Browser and Device Compatibility

AmplifyIQ will make reasonable efforts to build websites that function on modern commonly used browsers and devices at the time of development.

Exact appearance may vary across:

  • devices;
  • screen sizes;
  • operating systems; and
  • browsers.

Support for obsolete browsers, unusual hardware or legacy systems must be specifically agreed where required.

21. Search Engines and Digital Growth

Where AmplifyIQ provides SEO, digital-growth, advertising, conversion or related services, no specific commercial result is guaranteed unless expressly stated in writing.

AmplifyIQ cannot guarantee:

Where agreed, AmplifyIQ may use artificial-intelligence or automation tools as part of design, development, research, drafting, optimisation or production workflows.

Outputs used in a final client project will be subject to reasonable review appropriate to the service being supplied.

Clients remain responsible for reviewing and approving their final published business content, factual claims and industry-specific information.

23. Confidentiality

Each party should keep confidential information received from the other party confidential and use it only for purposes connected with the project.

This obligation does not apply to information that:

  • is already publicly available through no breach of these Terms;
  • was lawfully known before disclosure;
  • is independently developed;
  • is lawfully received from another source; or
  • must be disclosed by law.

24. Data Protection

Each party is responsible for complying with applicable data-protection obligations relevant to its role.

Where AmplifyIQ processes personal information on the client's behalf as a processor, the parties will enter into a Data Processing Agreement where required.

25. Cancellation by Business Clients

Unless a proposal states otherwise, a business client may request cancellation of a project by notifying AmplifyIQ in writing.

Where a business client cancels after work has commenced:

  • payments already made may be applied against work completed, committed project time and non-refundable third-party costs;
  • the client remains responsible for fees relating to work already performed;
  • the client remains responsible for authorised third-party expenses;
  • work completed beyond amounts already paid may be invoiced; and
  • any refund due will be calculated after the above amounts are taken into account.

Any project-specific cancellation terms contained within an accepted proposal will also apply.

26. Consumer Cancellation Rights

AmplifyIQ primarily provides services to businesses.

However, where a client legally qualifies as a consumer and enters into a distance or off-premises contract, the client may have statutory cancellation rights under Irish consumer law.

For many service contracts concluded at a distance, a consumer generally has a 14-day cancellation period beginning on the date the contract is concluded.

Where a consumer expressly asks AmplifyIQ to begin supplying services during the statutory cancellation period, the consumer may be required to pay an amount proportionate to services supplied before cancellation, where permitted by law.

Where applicable, AmplifyIQ will not seek to exclude or restrict statutory rights that cannot legally be excluded.

27. Suspension or Termination by AmplifyIQ

AmplifyIQ may suspend or terminate work where reasonably necessary, including where:

  • invoices remain overdue;
  • the client materially breaches the agreement;
  • the client requests unlawful activity;
  • required information is repeatedly withheld;
  • continued work creates an unreasonable security or legal risk; or
  • the client engages in abusive, threatening or seriously inappropriate conduct.

Where reasonably possible, AmplifyIQ will provide notice and an opportunity to resolve a remediable issue.

Amounts owed for work already completed remain payable.

28. Refunds

Refund entitlement depends on:

  • the project agreement;
  • the stage of the project;
  • work already completed;
  • third-party costs already incurred; and
  • any applicable statutory consumer rights.

A deposit is not automatically refundable merely because a client later changes their mind after work or reserved project time has commenced.

However, nothing in these Terms limits a refund or remedy to which a consumer is legally entitled.

To the maximum extent permitted by law, AmplifyIQ will not be responsible for indirect or consequential business losses arising from matters outside its reasonable control, including loss caused by:

Any limitation of liability must be interpreted subject to mandatory Irish law and any rights that cannot legally be excluded.

30. Force Majeure

Neither party will be responsible for delay or failure caused by circumstances outside its reasonable control.

These may include:

  • serious infrastructure failures;
  • widespread cyber incidents;
  • labour disputes;
  • war;
  • civil disturbance;
  • supplier failure; or
  • other events beyond reasonable control.

The affected party should make reasonable efforts to reduce the effect of the event.

Changes will not normally alter an existing signed or accepted project agreement retrospectively unless:

These Terms and any contract with AmplifyIQ are governed by the laws of Ireland, subject to any mandatory consumer protections that apply.
